title: Engine-Driven Generator

introduction.definition: An engine-driven generator uses a reciprocating engine to turn an AC generator. In a spark-ignition gas engine the fuel–air mixture is ignited by spark plugs; the pistons drive the crankshaft and flywheel, which turn the generator rotor. The governor holds constant speed so the frequency stays at 50/60 Hz.
key_points: Governor controls speed, AVR controls voltage
introduction.summary: An engine-driven generator uses a reciprocating engine as the prime mover to turn a generator. In this spark-ignition gas engine, fuel–air mixture burns in each cylinder and pushes the pistons down; the crankshaft turns the flywheel and the generator rotor, which induces AC voltage in the stator. The governor holds the speed constant so the frequency stays at 50 or 60 Hz.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Fuel gas train with pressure regulation; exhaust with silencer and flexible connection; ventilation for combustion and cooling air.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

overhaul.task: Engine top/major overhaul; alternator bearing replacement.

lubrication: Engine oil per maker (API/ACEA class); alternator bearings greased or sealed.

video_tutorials.title: Engine-Driven Generator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Engine-Driven Generator.
An engine-driven generator uses a reciprocating engine to turn an AC generator.
In a spark-ignition gas engine the fuel–air mixture is ignited by spark plugs; the pistons drive the crankshaft and flywheel, which turn the generator rotor.
The governor holds constant speed so the frequency stays at 50/60 Hz.
Typical applications include gas-engine CHP (combined heat and power); biogas and landfill-gas power; prime power in remote sites; peaking and grid support.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Flywheel with Starter Ring Gear, Generator – Rotor: 4 Salient Poles with Field Coils, Exciter Armature & Rotating Rectifier.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Engine-Driven Generator.
Check output voltage, frequency and alarms.
Check coolant, oil and fuel levels.
Change engine oil and filters; check belts and battery.
Measure generator insulation resistance.
Engine top/major overhaul; alternator bearing replacement.
Watch for engine misfire: rough running, power loss. Common cause: spark plug wear, ignition fault.
Watch for overheating: high coolant temperature. Common cause: blocked radiator, fan belt.
Watch for voltage instability: voltage hunting. Common cause: AVR fault.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
